kit/save — quit and resume a run

5 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Save layout and restored identitiesDeclaring the game blobSave, schema, and protocol versionsAPI by taskWorked excerpt (cavecrawl)Restore ordering and data lifetime

Use kit/save to save an authority's run to disk and restore it later. It uses the session backup snapshot and session_host_resume, which also support recovery after host loss. The backup sent every few seconds contains the session state needed to rehost; kit/save stores it in a versioned file alongside game-specific data. The package also creates persistent player tokens so returning players can reclaim their identities.

Saving operates at the session level for either replication model. The file contains delta-lane state and gd:"backup" data. It excludes simulation runtime history and inputs in flight: resuming a simulation save restarts the authority and initializes a fresh lane from saved authoritative fields. Live host migration supports only the cooperative lane; see sim.md.

Odin
import ksave "godot:kit/save"

Save layout and restored identities#

The file layout:

Code
[magic u32][format u16][game_version u16][saved_by u64][game blob][session snapshot]
  • format is the SDK's file-layout version, currently FORMAT :: u16(3). It changes with the session snapshot layout: version 2 added entity blobs and wire codecs; version 3 added the roster's admission state, locked and denied. Files from incompatible SDK versions return Bad_Envelope before their contents are interpreted.
  • game_version is the game's content version. The game supplies the value and decides which content changes require a new one.
  • saved_by records the saving host's Player_Id so it can resume under the same identity. Hosts have no reconnect token because they did not join as clients.
  • The game blob contains host-local data outside session identity, stats, and entities, such as wave directors, AI clocks, and quest flags. The game is responsible for saving that state.

Restore seats the caller as host in a lobby with the saved world loaded. Other players are disconnected but retain reclaimable identities. When they rejoin with persisted tokens, they recover their ids, stats, and owned entities through the normal reconnect path.

Envelope encoding and decoding are independent of Godot and can be unit-tested as bytes. File helpers wrap FileAccess so user:// paths work on every platform, including web.

Declaring the game blob#

Save the same host-local fields used for migration; see session. Tag them gd:"backup" on the game class. Scriptgen generates <class>_backup_write / _read with a field-layout version hash. Both takeover and disk resume can use that pair, keeping the write and read field lists in sync:

Odin
CaveLobby :: struct {
	host_ticks: int                           `gd:"backup"`,
	director:   kai.Director                  `gd:"backup"`, // serialize the complete POD struct
	brains:     map[knet.Net_Id]Dweller_Brain `gd:"backup"`, // map[POD]POD: serialize length, then entries
	respawn_at: map[knet.Net_Id]int           `gd:"backup"`,
	// ...
}

// the migration half (kboot.boot_migration's table calls it, host only):
@(gd_half)
cave_lobby_backup :: proc(self: ^CaveLobby, w: ^knet.Writer) {
	if self.started {cave_lobby_backup_write(self, w)}
}
// Read from a save file or the successor's `<game>_took_over(r)` half:
if !cave_lobby_backup_read(self, &r) { /* abort restore for incompatible or truncated data */ }

Supported fields are plain-data (POD) scalars, structs, fixed arrays, map[POD]POD, and [dynamic]POD, including fields reached through using and embeds as with replicate. Slices, strings, and non-POD elements produce build errors. The field-set hash lets a reader reject data from an incompatible build before interpreting it. For manually serialized fixed-layout state, knet.write_pod/read_pod expose the same primitive.

Save, schema, and protocol versions#

The repository uses three version checks for different data lifetimes:

  • Saved field data, including save files, gd:"backup" blobs, and succession payloads retained from an older build, uses a generated FNV field hash. A reader compares its layout with the writer's because the writer may no longer be available for negotiation. Scriptgen's <class>_backup_write/_read pair applies this check; knet.write_pod/read_pod expose it for manually serialized state.
  • Network messages use revision constants checked during admission. These include ksess.PROTOCOL_REV, knet.WIRE_REV, and revisions from each wire-bearing package, covering SES_* messages, the lane wire, and netgd frames. They contribute to the NET_FINGERPRINT sent in SES_JOIN. Incompatible peers receive Ev_Join_Denied{.Version} before exchanging deltas. Change the affected package's revision in the same commit as its wire format, and document the change beside the constant.
  • ksave.FORMAT versions the outer file envelope. It is maintained manually because it describes the fixed header and length-prefixed ranges rather than a generated field set: magic, format, game version, saving player id, game blob, and snapshot. Its format and changelog must remain readable before any inner version checks can run.

The migration wire wraps session_snapshot bytes as [blob_len u32][game blob][snapshot] without a second version field. PROTOCOL_REV already gates admission, and only admitted peers receive backups. The same snapshot stored on disk needs the save envelope because reading a file has no preceding join handshake.

Keep the two file-version errors distinct. Bad_Envelope means the SDK cannot read the FORMAT of the file. Wrong_Version means the game's game_version differs. A content-version change should not be reported as corrupt file data.

API by task#

Save (host only):

Odin
save_write :: proc(s: ^ksess.Session, w: ^knet.Writer, game_version: u16, game_blob: []u8 = nil)

Resume reads the file, validates the envelope and game version, and restores the run. It returns a temporary game-blob slice; parse it immediately:

Odin
resume :: proc(s: ^ksess.Session, name: string, path: cstring, game_version: u16) -> (game_blob: []u8, err: Resume_Error)

Resume_Error :: enum {
	Ok,
	No_File,       // nothing saved at `path`
	Bad_Envelope,  // incompatible magic or envelope format
	Wrong_Version, // a different game (or older content) wrote it
	Corrupt,       // the session snapshot didn't parse
}

Handle the error cases separately in player-facing status text; see the excerpt below. Custom slot UIs and save browsers can use the lower-level operations:

Odin
save_read_header :: proc(r: ^knet.Reader) -> (h: Header, ok: bool)
save_restore :: proc(s: ^ksess.Session, name: string, r: ^knet.Reader, h: Header) -> bool

save_read_header leaves the reader at the session snapshot for save_restore. It returns ok=false for incompatible magic or format, while the game must check game_version. save_restore requires a fresh session with its entity factory installed.

Identity uses a persisted token for reconnects, resumed saves, and entity reclamation:

Odin
persistent_token :: proc(path: cstring) -> u64

This loads the 8-byte token at path, or generates and persists one if needed. Retain the file and pass the same token to session_client_start on each run. The token is intended to resist guessing among invited friends; it is not a cryptographic authentication credential.

Files (user:// on every platform):

Odin
write_file :: proc(path: cstring, bytes: []u8) -> bool
file_exists :: proc(path: cstring) -> bool
read_file :: proc(path: cstring, allocator := context.allocator) -> (bytes: []u8, ok: bool)

Worked excerpt (cavecrawl)#

Saving writes the game blob first, then wraps the envelope around it.

Odin
blob := knet.writer_make()
defer knet.writer_destroy(&blob)
write_game_blob(self, &blob)
w := knet.writer_make()
defer knet.writer_destroy(&w)
ksave.save_write(&self.ses, &w, GAME_VERSION, knet.writer_bytes(&blob))
ok := ksave.write_file(save_path(), knet.writer_bytes(&w))

On resume, handle errors first, restore the game blob, then start the transport:

Odin
blob, err := ksave.resume(&self.ses, my_name(self), save_path(), GAME_VERSION)
switch err {
case .No_File:
    kui.lobby_set_status(&self.ui, "No saved run to resume")
    return
case .Bad_Envelope, .Wrong_Version:
    kui.lobby_set_status(&self.ui, "That save is from another cave")
    return
case .Corrupt:
    return
case .Ok:
}
if !read_game_blob(self, blob) {return}
if !gd.host(self.owner, port()) {return}   // transport starts after restore; see ordering constraints

Identity gets wired at join time (net.odin):

Odin
ksess.session_client_start(&self.ses, my_token(), my_name(self))
// my_token() -> ksave.persistent_token("user://cave_token")
// (tests choose an identity via a CAVE_TOKEN env override instead)

Restore ordering and data lifetime#

  • Transport order is flexible. ksave.resume can run before or after transport setup because nothing sends until the session ticks. If transport setup fails after resume, the restored session can be abandoned. The next session_host_start / session_client_start reinitializes it.
  • Save private host state in the blob. Without it, Cavecrawl restarts wave 1 alongside the saved dwellers because the session restores entities without restoring the wave director.
  • Parse the temporary blob promptly. The slice returned by resume views temporary file bytes and becomes invalid when the temporary allocator resets.
  • Install the factory before restore. Restore recreates every entity through session_set_factory; a fresh session needs that factory first.
  • save_write asserts is_host: only the authority saves the run.
  • Bump game_version when game content changes; Cavecrawl uses GAME_VERSION :: u16(9). SDK envelope mismatches return Bad_Envelope; game-version mismatches return Wrong_Version.
